# Behavioral Specification: TL-UL to SRAM Adapter

## 1. Overview

This module bridges a TileLink-UL (TL-UL) request/response interface to a simple SRAM-like memory interface. It accepts TL-UL read and write transactions, translates them into SRAM accesses, and forms the corresponding TL-UL responses.

The SRAM-like interface has:

- a request/grant handshake,
- a write-enable output,
- word-addressed address output,
- write data and write-mask outputs,
- read data, read-data-valid, and read-error inputs.

The SRAM-like interface does **not** provide a write-acknowledge; write responses are therefore generated by the adapter itself once the write has been accepted.

The adapter is parameterizable in:

- SRAM address width,
- SRAM data width,
- maximum number of outstanding transactions,
- whether sub-word / byte accesses are allowed,
- whether writes are globally rejected,
- whether reads are globally rejected.

## 2. Reset and Idle Behavior

- After reset, the adapter shall be idle.
- In the idle state, it shall not assert a response, shall not assert an SRAM request, and shall drive SRAM control/data outputs to defined idle values.
- No response shall be generated for a transaction that was not accepted on the TL-UL request channel.

## 3. Request Acceptance

- A TL-UL request is accepted only when the request-valid and request-ready handshake completes.
- The adapter shall assert request-ready only when it is able to record the transaction and, for a transaction that will access the SRAM, the SRAM grants access.
- A request that is rejected as an error may be accepted without an SRAM grant. Such a request shall not cause any SRAM access.
- The adapter shall not accept more outstanding transactions than its configured maximum outstanding limit.
- Accepted requests shall eventually receive exactly one response.

## 4. Address Mapping

- The SRAM interface is word-addressed.
- The adapter shall derive the SRAM address from the TL-UL byte address by removing the low bits needed to address a byte within the configured SRAM data word.
- For example, with a 32-bit SRAM data width, the low two address bits are not used as part of the SRAM word address.
- The adapter does not perform base-address decode. Address bits above the SRAM address range are ignored. Therefore, accesses to addresses outside the SRAM range may alias to SRAM locations.

## 5. SRAM Request Generation

- For every accepted, non-error request, the adapter shall issue an SRAM request and keep it asserted until the SRAM grant is observed.
- For read requests, the SRAM write-enable shall be deasserted.
- For write requests, the SRAM write-enable shall be asserted.
- The SRAM address, write data, and write mask shall be presented as part of the SRAM request.
- When no SRAM request is active, the SRAM address, write data, write mask, and write-enable outputs shall be deterministic idle values.

## 6. Write Transactions

- A valid write request shall be forwarded to the SRAM as a write access.
- The adapter shall not wait for a write-acknowledge from the SRAM.
- After a write request has been accepted, the adapter shall generate a write-response (`AccessAck`).
- The write-response shall echo the request’s source identifier and size.
- The write-response shall have no error bit asserted unless the request was rejected due to an error condition.

## 7. Read Transactions

- A valid read request shall be forwarded to the SRAM as a read access.
- The adapter shall hold the response until the SRAM returns read data with read-data-valid.
- The adapter shall then generate a read-data response (`AccessAckData`).
- The read-data response shall echo the request’s source identifier and size.
- The read-data response shall contain the SRAM read data gated by the original request’s byte-lane mask. Byte lanes not requested shall be returned as zero.
- If the SRAM reports an uncorrectable read error, the read-data response shall have the error bit asserted.
- A correctable read error indication shall be ignored and shall not cause a response error.

## 8. Byte-Lane and Data Masking

- The TL-UL request provides byte-lane enables.
- For write accesses, the adapter shall expand each byte-lane enable to an all-ones byte in the SRAM write mask. A disabled byte lane shall produce an all-zero byte in the SRAM write mask.
- For write data, the adapter shall drive valid data only on enabled byte lanes. Disabled byte lanes shall be driven to zero.
- For read responses, only bytes corresponding to enabled byte lanes of the original request shall be taken from SRAM read data. All other response bytes shall be zero.

## 9. Response Ordering and Response Fields

- The adapter shall return responses in the same order as the corresponding requests were accepted.
- A write request shall produce `AccessAck`.
- A read request shall produce `AccessAckData`.
- The response source and size shall match the original request.
- Unused or reserved response fields shall be driven to zero.

## 10. Error Handling

The adapter shall reject invalid requests with an error response and shall not perform an SRAM access for those requests.

The following shall be treated as request errors:

- undefined or illegal TL-UL opcodes,
- request size larger than the configured data width,
- address not aligned to the request size,
- byte mask inconsistent with the request size,
- invalid mask combinations as defined by TL-UL protocol rules,
- full-data write requests with an invalid mask,
- reads or writes prohibited by the adapter’s configuration.

Response behavior for rejected requests:

- If the rejected request is a write-type request, the response shall be `AccessAck` with the error bit asserted.
- If the rejected request is a read-type request, the response shall be `AccessAckData` with the error bit asserted and zero read data.
- The response shall still echo the request’s source and size.

The adapter shall not issue an SRAM request for any rejected request.

## 11. Configuration-Dependent Behavior

### 11.1 Byte Access Disabled

- Writes shall be allowed only if they access the full configured data width.
- Any write with a size smaller than the full data width, or with fewer than all byte lanes enabled, shall be rejected with an error.
- Read accesses may still use sub-word byte-lane masks; read responses shall be masked accordingly.

### 11.2 Writes Globally Rejected

- When writes are disabled by configuration, every write request shall be rejected with an error response.
- No SRAM write access shall be issued.

### 11.3 Reads Globally Rejected

- When reads are disabled by configuration, every read request shall be rejected with an error response.
- No SRAM read access shall be issued.

### 11.4 Invalid Configuration

- The configuration shall not enable both global write rejection and global read rejection; such a configuration would make the adapter unable to perform any valid transaction.

## 12. External SRAM Behavior

The adapter assumes that the SRAM side obeys the following behavior:

- A grant is required before the SRAM accepts a request.
- Read-data-valid is asserted only when read data for a previously accepted read request is available.
- The SRAM read-error status is provided with the read data.

The adapter uses the SRAM read-error status only to determine whether the read response shall be marked as an error.
